page: Microsoft Azure E64-16ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EADSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 8 physical cores with multi-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high resource density of 32.0 GB of memory per core.

This server includes 2458 GB of local NVMe storage and is Premium Storage capable, making it suitable for data-intensive operations. In benchmark evaluations, the processor demonstrates strong single-core performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 2916.18. Multi-core CPU performance and software compilation benchmarks fall within the average tier. Notably, the server exhibits strong performance in text generation for small language models, reaching 277.6 tokens per second.

While cached memory bandwidth is average at 1045.32 GB/sec, a key hardware tradeoff is observed in uncached memory operations. Large-block read and write memory bandwidth benchmarks are weak, registering at 38.96 GB/sec and 22.66 GB/sec respectively. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and integrated local storage offer a dense resource profile that reduces the need for external storage attachments for large datasets, though workloads requiring sustained high-throughput uncached memory access may experience bottlenecks.

The E64-16ads_v5 is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads that benefit from local scratch space. Appropriate use cases include relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data analytics, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
